articles.title: Corktown collision involving cyclist, police car sends 1 person to hospital
articles.summary: One person was transported to a hospital on Wednesday afternoon following a collision involving a cyclist and a police car. Authorities say the crash happened in the Corktown area, near King Street East and Parliament Street, just before 5 p.m. The extent of the victim’s injuries was not immediately known. articles.title: Subway service resumes on stretch of Line 2 Bloor-Danforth after power outage
articles.summary: The TTC says subway service on Line 2 between Woodbine and Broadview stations has resumed after a brief disruption due to a power outage. There’s no word on what caused the outage, which lasted roughly 25 minutes during the afternoon rush.

articles.title: Ford, Joly call on Stellantis to make new model at Brampton plant after automaker signals potential sale
articles.summary: Ontario Premier Doug Ford and federal Industry Minister Mélanie Joly are calling on Stellantis to produce a new model at its idled Brampton, Ont., assembly plant after the automaker signed a memorandum of understanding (MOU) with Canadian armoured vehicle maker Roshel on its potential sale.

articles.title: Unifor urges government to prevent sale of Stellantis’ Brampton, Ont., plant
articles.summary: The union representing Canadian workers at Stellantis is urging the federal government to intervene as the automaker looks to sell its idled Brampton, Ont., assembly plant to Canadian armoured ⁠vehicle maker Roshel.

articles.title: Worker dead after being struck by commercial truck in Brampton: police
articles.summary: A man has died in an industrial accident after being struck by a truck during road work, according to Peel Regional Police.

articles.title: Male struck by vehicle during road work in Brampton has died: Peel police
articles.summary: Peel Regional Police say a worker struck by a vehicle while doing road repairs in Brampton on Wednesday afternoon has died. Emergency crews were called to the intersection of Countryside Drive and The Gore Road at around 1:28 p.m. Investigators say the male worker was struck by a commercial truck. He was later pronounced dead. […]

articles.title: Crown drops charge against Toronto man accused in Pearson airport gold heist
articles.summary: Prosecutors have withdrawn a charge against a Toronto man accused of taking part in the multimillion-dollar gold heist at Pearson airport in 2023.

articles.title: Hold and secure lifted from 9 Riverdale schools: Toronto police
articles.summary: A hold and secure has been lifted from nine schools in the Riverdale area on Wednesday afternoon. Police told CityNews that officers were on scene investigating at a school in the neighbourhood due to a threat that was received by a student. articles.title: Ford supports Carney's plan for private investors Toronto's Pearson airport
articles.summary: Ontario Premier Doug Ford is fully on board with the prime minister's plan to see private investors take over operations at Canada's four largest airports, including Toronto Pearson, he said Wednesday.

articles.title: Mississauga city council votes to block data centre projects for 1 year
articles.summary: Mississauga city council has voted unanimously on a moratorium on new data centres for one year, the latest municipality to hit the brakes on the artificial intelligence-fuelled build out.

articles.title: Tell us what changes you want to see in Durham Region this election
articles.summary: CBC Oshawa wants to know what's shaping your vote, so we can cover the stories you care about.

articles.title: Sanofi launching $925M vaccine manufacturing facility in North York
articles.summary: French pharmaceutical company Sanofi officially launched its new $925 million vaccine manufacturing facility in North York on Wednesday — a site that will be used to create high-dose flu vaccines for seniors in Canada.

articles.title: Venue shortages and city growth take centre stage at Brampton mayoral town hall
articles.summary: Five candidates vying to lead Brampton took the stage together for the first time in the 2026 municipal election campaign on Tuesday night.

articles.title: Second Harvest opens Etobicoke food processing facility for school programs
articles.summary: As back-to-school season takes full effect, a Canada-wide organization that rescues surplus food from suppliers and retailers is opening a new food processing facility in Etobicoke for school programs. Second Harvest will take food that would otherwise be bound for landfills, and repurpose into healthy snacks for students.

articles.title: Oshawa funeral home fire was arson, police say
articles.summary: The cause of a fire at Mcintosh-Anderson-Kellam Funeral Home in downtown Oshawa earlier this month was arson, investigators said in an update Tuesday.

articles.title: Teen killed in shooting near Jane and Finch remembered as 'young king' with bright future ahead
articles.summary: A 17-year-old boy fatally shot in Toronto on Monday is being remembered as a "young king" whose future has been abruptly taken away by gun violence.
